data.why: The app ships its own example feature table and metadata (data/raw/example_feature_table.csv, data/raw/feature_metadata.csv) regenerated deterministically (seed=42) by run_pipeline.py during install, which also trains and saves models/screening_bundle.joblib that the Streamlit app requires at startup; the app's own sidebar upload/download buttons let the browser get and resubmit this same synthetic file, so no external test files are needed.

goals: Screen a batch of newborn LC-HR-MS feature-table samples and see which are called high risk vs low risk
For each high-risk sample, inspect the key abnormal analytes (robust z-scores) and the suspected disorder before referring for confirmatory testing
Compare the two-tier screen (cut-off plus ML re-ranking) against the classic single-marker cut-off to see the reduction in false-positive recalls
Act as the human-in-the-loop specialist: confirm, reject as an analytical artefact, or request a repeat sample for each flagged case, and export the audit trail
Upload a different/edited feature table (e.g. the downloaded example, modified) to see how the pipeline's calls change

review.summary: The tree describes the app accurately: run a two-tier newborn IEM screen on an LC-HR-MS feature table, triage the flagged samples by abnormal analytes, then record expert confirm, reject or repeat decisions in an exportable audit trail. The labels are good and most evidence holds up, but two citations (017 and 030) don't show what their nodes claim, the upload goal has no task node, and two tasks are general grid operations, so it needs small fixes before filing.
